question: can this lane satisfy the NPU decode-graph adapter contract, and how large is the integration?
answer: the contract is satisfiable and the integration is a single reversible constructor call. No launcher surgery is required, which is much cheaper than the earlier estimate.

contract_checked_before_spending_a_model.constructor_gate: NpuDecodeGraphs.__init__ refuses unless _reference_reduction_enabled(), i.e. unless POCKETLLM_V41_MMA_EMULATE is not disabled.
contract_checked_before_spending_a_model.this_lane: env.sh does not set POCKETLLM_V41_MMA_EMULATE at all, and kernels.quantized_linear documents emulation as ON by default. So the gate passes.
block_gates: _require_capturable_block: every non host-side parameter and buffer of a block must be on the capture device. This lane is device-resident, so it should pass.

_require_staged_quantized_modules: a module marked quantized must have at least one linear carrying the file's E4M3 codes and E8M0 grid, which is what proves the original-byte staging ran. The lane loads through loader.load_backbone on the NPU device, which is that staging.
contract_checked_before_spending_a_model.so: no gate refuses this lane on inspection. A capture attempt is worth a run.

the_integration_point.mechanism: DecodeGraphs.__init__ walks model.layers and does `graphs = LayerGraphs(block, self.pool, warmup)` then `block.decode_graph = graphs` (graphs.py:434-435). Block.forward reads that one attribute.
the_integration_point.activation: constructing NpuDecodeGraphs(model) is the whole opt-in: no CLI flag and no environment variable selects it, by design.
the_integration_point.recording: graphs.capture_pass(model_forward) runs the model forward once; the first reach of each layer records instead of replaying, and the caches are rewound afterwards so the following step is the one the eager column would have taken.
the_integration_point.reversal: release() sets block.decode_graph back to None, and the docstring says a layer that outlives the graphs then runs the eager body again. So the change is one assignment and reverting it is one assignment.
the_integration_point.why_this_matters: the earlier estimate assumed the launcher would need patching. It does not: the launcher constructs the model and drives steps, so adoption is one constructor before the timed loop plus one capture_pass call.

what_the_capture_would_still_have_to_sto: every layer must be replayable as two recordings plus the eager middle, so the per-forward dispatch closure from _forward_for(shard) (Python lock, installed-flag check) runs between the two recordings
the shared pool must hold forty layers of recordings at once; pool_bytes is reported precisely because it is the pool size and not a per-layer figure
capture_pass needs one real decode step, so it must run after the caches exist and before timing
why_the_run_was_not_started_this_round: a capture attempt is a full eight-rank model load plus the capture pass, which is well past the remaining budget for this round. Starting it and being cut off would leave a leased host with a half-run job, which the release discipline forbids.
what_is_not_claimed: no capture was attempted, no parity measured, no speedup claimed. The objective gate stands unchanged: full eight ranks, complete 64 steps, FP32 bit-identical against the eager lane as control, before any gain is believed.
next: construct NpuDecodeGraphs on the loaded model, call capture_pass with one real step, report whether it records and the reported pool_bytes; then run the parity gate. If the capture refuses, record the named refusal verbatim.
method: read-only source analysis; no model run, no code change
